doc.name: bidcatch
doc.instructions:
WHAT THIS SERVER IS. BidCatch tracks US government contracting end to end: open and past bids from federal, state, county, city, school district, and port authority portals; federal award history; contracts nearing expiration (recompetes); agency procurement forecasts; and GAO bid-protest decisions. Every record links back to the official government posting — cite that link, not BidCatch, when the user needs a source. Paid tools add prime–subcontractor teaming networks and structured award filtering.

HOW TO SEARCH WELL. (1) Search by classification codes, not just keywords: NAICS classifies the work (541512 = computer systems design, 237310 = highway/street/bridge, 561720 = janitorial); FSC/PSC codes classify federal supplies and services. Ask the user for their codes, or infer them from their trade and confirm. (2) Match the buyer level: a paving crew bids county and city work, not SAM.gov — use the state and level filters rather than scanning federal-only. (3) Check deadlines before presenting anything: a bid with a past response deadline is a dead end; say so. (4) Award history is intelligence: before a user bids, run get_award_history on the buyer or incumbent to see who wins this work and for how much. (5) Read the recompete clock: get_recompete_radar shows contracts expiring soon — the strongest opportunities are the ones not yet posted. (6) Check the fight record: get_protest_record reveals whether a buyer's awards get challenged and overturned.

TOOL MAP. search_bids = current and past opportunities. get_award_history = who won what, from which agency, for how much. get_recompete_radar = contracts nearing expiration, ranked by recompete signals with the counts behind them. get_agency_forecast = purchases agencies have announced but not yet posted. get_protest_record = GAO protest rulings (sustained = the agency had to back down; denied = the award stood). check_exclusions = SAM.gov's debarment list — run it on any company before the user teams with or subcontracts to them; one excluded partner can poison a bid. find_teaming_partners = who a company teams with — the primes it subs for and the subs under it, from prime-reported subcontract records. search_awards = structured award filtering by recipient, agency, NAICS, state, and single-bid awards — use it when the user knows exactly which slice they want; get_award_history when they're searching by topic.

HONEST LIMITS. Ceiling values are maximums, not spending — never sum them into market-size claims; record counts are the honest aggregate. A posted forecast or an expiring contract is a signal, not a guarantee — agencies slip and cancel. Teaming relationships are reported by primes to USAspending/FSRS — counts are reported records and amounts are per-record, never summed; subcontract reporting is known to undercount small subs. Classified work is not visible in public data. If a search returns nothing, widen the keywords or drop a filter before concluding no work exists.

tools.name: search_bids
tools.description: Search government bid opportunities (open and past) by keyword, state, and buyer level. Results are relevance-ranked; keyword matches in the title outrank passing mentions in the description. Optionally filter by set-aside program (set_asides).

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX

open_only.description: true = only bids whose deadline has not passed

set_asides.description: Set-aside programs, any of which matches: SDVOSB, VOSB, HUBZone, 8(a), EDWOSB, WOSB, DVBE, DBE, MBE, WBE, SBE, HUB, SDB, SBS; 'none' = the record says no set-aside was used (unrestricted). Many records are not marked either way, so a set-aside search never returns them.

tools.name: get_award_history
tools.description: Search federal contract award history — who won what, for how much, and when. Use it to size up incumbents, price work, or find buyers. amount: the award's current value; null = no current value reported (never the ceiling). Requires a BidCatch intel key.

query.description: Keywords matched against description, recipient, and agency

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX

tools.name: get_recompete_radar
tools.description: List federal contracts nearing expiration — each one a competition about to reopen. Filter by keyword, NAICS code, or state. Requires a BidCatch intel key.

query.description: Keywords matched against description, recipient, and agency

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX

tools.name: get_agency_forecast
tools.description: List an agency's published procurement forecast — planned contract actions with estimated values and timelines, in the agency's own words. Planning-grade data; entries can be revised or cancelled. Requires a BidCatch intel key.

agency.description: Agency name or distinctive fragment, e.g. 'Interior' or 'Veterans'

tools.name: get_protest_record
tools.description: Search Government Accountability Office (GAO) bid protest decisions — who challenged an award, and whether the referee sustained or denied it. Requires a BidCatch intel key.

query.description: Keywords matched against agency and case matter

tools.name: check_exclusions
tools.description: Check SAM.gov's exclusion (debarment) list for a company or person — entities the government has barred from receiving federal contracts or subcontracts. Run this before teaming with or subcontracting to anyone: one excluded partner can poison a bid. Match by exact company name or UEI; a state filter disambiguates common names. Records come from SAM.gov's published exclusions extract, refreshed weekly.

name.description: Company or person name, e.g. 'Acme Paving LLC'

uei.description: SAM.gov Unique Entity ID — the strongest match key

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX

tools.name: find_teaming_partners
tools.description: Find who a company teams with on federal contracts — the primes it subcontracts for and the subcontractors under it. Built from prime-reported subcontract records (USAspending/FSRS): real reported relationships, not guesses. Use it before a recompete to map an incumbent's bench, or to find primes a subcontractor already works with. Requires a BidCatch intel key.

company.description: Company name, e.g. 'Booz Allen Hamilton' — resolved to the strongest match

uei.description: SAM.gov Unique Entity ID — the strongest match key

role.description: prime = only partners they sub FOR; sub = only subs UNDER them; omit for both

tools.name: search_awards
tools.description: Filter federal contract awards by exact fields — recipient, awarding agency, NAICS code, state — instead of keyword search. Includes a single-bid filter for awards that drew exactly one offer. Use this when you know the slice you want; use get_award_history for topic/keyword search. Can filter by set-aside program (set_asides). amount: the award's current value; null = no current value reported (never the ceiling). Requires a BidCatch intel key.

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX

one_bid_only.description: true = only awards that received exactly one offer

set_asides.description: Set-aside programs, any of which matches: SDVOSB, VOSB, HUBZone, 8(a), EDWOSB, WOSB, DVBE, DBE, MBE, WBE, SBE, HUB, SDB, SBS; 'none' = the record says no set-aside was used (unrestricted). Many records are not marked either way, so a set-aside search never returns them.
